/LILIAN

Baltic Exchange Market Report 23 June 2026
Baltic Dry Index: 2667 (-17)
Baltic Capesize Index: 4046 (-28)
Baltic Panamax Index: 2045 (-14)
Baltic Supramax Index: 1705 (-10)
Baltic Handysize Index: 941 (5)
CAPESIZE
The market gave back some ground on Tuesday, with the BCI 182 5TC slipping by $252 to close at $36,695. In the Pacific sentiment eased despite healthy operator enquiry from both West Coast Australia and East Coast Australia. Two major miners were active on C5, but this was insufficient to generate further upward momentum. Bids opened the day around $11.00 before fixtures were concluded at $11.65, leaving the route relatively unchanged overall, with C5 slipping $0.215 to settle at $11.660. The Atlantic remained the brighter spot. The improved momentum that emerged late last week carried over into yesterday, supported by increased activity from South Brazil and West Africa into China. Reports overnight indicated fixtures concluded at $32.50 on two occasions before a further fixture at $32.95 for 15/20 July loading. However, sentiment cooled slightly during today’s trading, with bids easing back towards $32.00 and offers narrowing to around $32.75. Despite this, C3 edged $0.211 higher to close at $32.361.
PANAMAX
Brokers reported mixed views on the direction of the Atlantic basin, although there is broad agreement that activity had increased today. Market sources noted an increase in fresh cargo volumes across both fronthaul and trans Atlantic trades, with a widening spread developing as owners maintain firmer offers. In general tonnage and cargo supply is considered to be relatively well balanced, however market participants highlighted pockets of prompt tonnage tightness in the North Continent and West Mediterranean, which could lead to the occasional fixture being concluded at stronger levels. The Yasa Eagle (81,526 2012) open Krishnapatnam 12 June was reported to have been placed on subjects for an EC South America fronthaul, and the Olivia C (81,800 2015) open in Paradip 20 June was said to have fixed for a similiar trade direction, but no further details surfaced for either. The CL Shangrao (82,372 2024) open in Pecem 10 July was reported as fixed but no other information was heard. ETG were said to have fixed the BH Power (82,197 2024) basis passing Sunda Strait 28 June for an EC South America fronthaul at $22,000. In the Pacific sentiment remains somewhat negative, although there are indications that the recent downward pressure on rates is beginning to ease. Owners are said to be increasingly showing resistance, particularly on certain trade routes, with stronger pushback evident from larger and more modern vessels. The P5TC slipped a further $126 to $18,406.
SUPRAMAX
The market in both Basins took a pause today. There appeared to be a stand-off in the US Gulf with Owners remaining optimistic and market becoming very positional, whilst elsewhere in the Atlantic it just felt like the market taking breather as a reaction to the recent gains. Brokers said that own tonnage was being nominated more for stems now, with arbitrages less likely. The Asian market remained subdued with the bid/offer spread widening with a lack of fresh enquiry and very few reported trades. Cargill were said to have fixed the Karo T (63,520 2023) Koh Sichang 24 June for a trip via South China redelivery West Africa in the high $17,000’s, but the exact details remained elusive. The 11TC dropped $122 to close at $21,552.
HANDYSIZE
The market maintained a steady tone overall, with no major shift in sentiment. The BHSI closed the day at 941, while the 7TC average inched up by $92 to settle at $16,931. In the Continent and Mediterranean limited activity was reported with rates holding broadly flat. The South Atlantic and US Gulf continued to display a firm outlook, with market dynamics stable and fixtures surfacing above last done levels. In Asia conditions also remained stable, with a balanced cargo-to-tonnage ratio keeping rates largely unchanged.

Atlantic
A 38,000-dwt was heard fixed for a trip delivery Recalada to Egypt at $24,000, although further details were not disclosed.

Asia
The Charisma.GR (37,295 2019) open Yokohama spot was fixed to the Continent via COGH at around $17,000, although further details were lacking. The Shinsung Accord (37,063 2015) open Mundra on/or around 25–30 June was heard fixed for two to three laden legs, although further details were not disclosed.

Market Fundamentals
World Crude Steel Production

World crude steel output eased 0.4% y-o-y to 157.8 Mt in May, bringing Jan-May production down 1.5% at 772.8 Mt, World Steel Association data show. In May, Asian steel production dropped 0.8% to 115.8 Mt as China remained the drag, down 2.7% to 84.4 Mt. In contrast, output rose in India (+1.9% to 14.1 Mt), Japan (+1.7% to 7.0 Mt) and South Korea (+3.3% to 5.4 Mt). Meanwhile, North American steel production rose 11.5% in May, as Canadian and US production climbed 31.4% and 9.2% on the year to a respective 1.0 Mt and 7.5 Mt.

Trading Commentary
Cape
The Cape FFA curve was supported today, despite the index losing another $252, with the Jul making the biggest gains trading up to 30050. The Aug was close behind with a high of 31150 paid, as the Jul v Aug spread narrows and strengthens up to -1000 in good volume. Q3 made significant gains also with 31400 paid, with a large portion of the volume was traded via the Q3 v Q4 at -1600. The Q4 range was 32400-32750 and Cal27 27000-27200. More surprisingly the Cal28 contract was one of the biggest moves with 23900 paid multiple times.

PMX
PMX market saw strength across the curve today, with activity concentrated in the front months. Jul traded heavily from an early low of 17,900 before rallying steadily through the day to print highs of 19,000. The bulk of volume traded between 18,400 and 18,900. Aug traded from a low of 18,150 to highs of 19,100 while sep printed in a narrower range from 18,650 pushing to 19,100 at close, the Aug+Sep strip improved to 19,000. Further out, Q3 traded actively from 18,250 up to 19,000. Q4 saw solid liquidity, lifting from 17,900 to 18,300 and finishing the day around that level. Deferred interest was limited, with Cal 27 seeing a single large print at 15,475 and Cal 28 trading repeatedly at 14,450

ai_analysis.summary: BDI下跌17点至2667，各船型指数涨跌互现。Capesize大西洋市场表现优于太平洋，C3航线小幅上涨0.211至32.361。Panamax市场活动回升，北欧和西地中海即期运力趋紧，但太平洋仍承压。Supramax进入盘整，亚洲市场清淡。Handysize指数微涨5点至941，市场整体平稳。FFA曲线显示即期下跌但远期合同普遍走强，交易活跃度提升。

sections.title: Market Structure
sections.content: 干散货市场整体回调但结构分化。Capesize大西洋表现强劲，巴西至中国航线（C3）上涨，因南巴西和西非至中国货盘增加。太平洋市场情绪降温，C5航线下滑。Panamax市场活跃度上升，即期运力紧张支撑大西洋费率，但太平洋仍由租家主导。Supramax进入盘整，亚洲缺乏新鲜询盘。Handysize保持稳定，大西洋和美湾维持坚挺。FFA曲线近月走弱但Q3及远期合同普遍上涨，显示市场对中期前景仍持乐观态度。

sections.title: Dry Bulk Signals
sections.content: 积极信号：Capesize大西洋C3航线逆势上扬，西非至中国货盘活跃；Panamax大西洋新鲜货量增加，运力供需趋紧；Supramax美湾船东心态乐观；Handysize 7TC平均上涨92美元。消极信号：Capesize太平洋C5航线下跌0.215美元；Panamax太平洋P5TC继续下滑126美元；Supramax亚洲市场持续低迷。FFA交易显示Jul合同大幅反弹，Cape涨525美元，Panamax涨700美元，反映市场对短期回调后反弹的预期。

sections.title: Trading Focus
sections.content: 建议关注：Capesize C3航线（32.00-33.50 offer）大西洋持续活跃机会；Panamax跨大西洋航线（P1A_82）费率支撑较强；Handysize美湾和南大西洋航线坚挺。FFA市场Jul合同交易活跃度显著，Cape和Panamax曲线前月大幅反弹，可关注跨月价差机会。Pacific市场下行压力趋缓，部分船东开始抵制低价，密切关注运力平衡变化。

market_watch: Capesize C3大西洋航线货盘活跃，即期费率支撑较强，短期或维持坚挺
Panamax大西洋运力趋紧，北欧和西地中海即期船供给减少，费率易涨难跌
Supramax亚洲市场清淡，运力过剩压力持续，但美湾市场信心回升
Handysize大西洋和美湾维持稳定，太平洋市场平衡，费率整体平稳
FFA曲线Q3至Q4合同普遍上涨，远期市场信心增强，显示对中期干散货需求持乐观态度

route_focus.view: 巴西至中国航线（大西洋核心航线）：收盘32.361美元/吨，小幅上涨0.211美元。近期南巴西和西非至中国货盘活跃支撑费率。短期情绪降温但C3仍保持相对强势，注意32.00-33.50区间波动。短期支撑32.00，阻力33.50。
跨大西洋航线（Panamax基准航线）：Transatlantic RV报19,355-20,500美元/天（租家-船东），船东报价显著高于租家报价。运力供需相对平衡但即期运力趋紧支撑船东立场。中期（Q3 26）FFA报19,000-19,100，低于即期市场，暗示市场预期季节性走弱。关注7月谷物出货节奏。
Skaw至Passero经里约热内卢-Recalada航线（Handysize大西洋航线）：报7,461美元/天，上涨54美元。市场活动有限但费率小幅攀升。南大西洋和美湾市场维持坚挺，Handysize整体平稳。大西洋航线供需健康，短期或维持当前水平。
